title: Two queues: FCFS above, RR below
summary: High priority runs FCFS; low priority shares the CPU in round robin; a high process preempts a low one.
hints: The priority of a process is its queue: `0` high, `1` low. The line of a process is `arrival queue k burst1 ... burstk`.
For the head of the queue use a number smaller than all the others (a counter that goes down), so the same 'smallest first' rule finds it.
A high process is never preempted: its quantum is as good as infinite.
